Dr. Tracey Coleman is an accomplished leader that began her career as a manager in fortune 500 companies. She received her Bachelor’s Degree in Organizational Management, Masters in Leadership and Management, and her Doctorate in Management of Organizational Leadership. Dr. Coleman’s journey in education consist of management consultant, educational consultant, adjunct faculty, tenured faculty, and currently dean. She has enjoyed the educational journey providing needed support to students and continues to mentor many of those whom she instructed in the classroom. The work in her consulting business has allowed her to continue on the path of teaching and development of others. Dr. Coleman is an advocate for students, their education and success, as well as the ability for them to become effective members of society.
Dr. Coleman considers her work to reflect the leader within, a servant leader who utilizes her talents to effect change in others, by being the change.

excerpts.line: Dean of Academic Pathways and Student Success
window: Dr. Luis Escobar has more than 18 years of experience in higher education in a wide range of positions including Classified Professional, Counseling faculty, Dean of Counseling and most recently as the Vice President of Student Services at Chabot College. His academic journey started as a community college first generation student. As a Latino male, raised in an immigrant family where he was the first to graduate from an institution of higher learning, his drive and commitment to advancing equitable student success outcomes stems from a deep personal connection to issues of educational equity.

Dr. Escobar earned his Associate Degree from Contra Costa College, Bachelor of Arts in Psychology, Masters of Science in Counseling, and Doctorate in Educational Leadership from San Francisco State University.
Dean of Academic Pathways and Student Success

Hello! I have been a full time counselor since 2016 and prior to that, a high school counselor in San Leandro Unified for 10 years. I earned my BA in International Relations with a minor in Spanish from UC Davis and my MS in Counseling with concentrations in School and College Counseling from San Francisco State University.
As a first generation college student myself, I understand the experience of being the first in your family to attend college and I strive to provide the best support to all students.

Dean of Counseling \r\nLMFT #44742 and LPCC #1702 \r\nI believe in the power of student advocacy, challenging mental health stigmas and weaving the equity framework in everything I do. I am a lifelong learner, believe in holistic well-being and enjoy collaborating to support student success! Prior to joining the student services administrator team, I was a full time counselor/instructor at Chabot for 17 years (Aug. 2005-June 2022). I hold an MA in Counseling Psychology with a dual emphasis in career counseling and marriage family therapy and presently pursuing my doctorate in Community Care and Counseling with a focus in Traumatology.

Matthew Lee serves as Dean of Health, Kinesiology, and Athletics at Chabot College, where he leads programs in health sciences, nursing, dental hygiene, emergency medical services, kinesiology, physical education, and intercollegiate athletics.

He is committed to advancing student success, equitable access, and career and transfer pathways through strong academic programs, student-centered support, and community partnerships. His leadership focuses on collaboration, innovation, and creating opportunities that help students achieve their educational and professional goals.

“I’ve seen first-hand how integrated tutoring operations and learning communities cultivate college-readiness among marginalized and underrepresented students. I’m thrilled to work at Chabot as we re-imagine what a truly accessible and just college looks and feels like.”

Paul lives in Fairview (between Hayward and Castro Valley) with his wife Rhee and their dog Domino. Their son Donovan is an aspiring geologist currently studying at Sonoma State. He has acted and directed community theatre productions and plays soccer and disc golf when he can.
